title: Detectability of λ through readings: unit, direction, common now, order

key_results.statement: Statistics of a schedule: $P(s_1,\dots,s_K)=\lVert\Pi^{(K)}_{s_K}(\lambda_K)\cdots\Pi^{(1)}_{s_1}(\lambda_1)\Psi_0\rVert^2$ with $X(\lambda)=e^{iC\lambda}Xe^{-iC\lambda}$; factors at equal $\lambda$ commute, so their order does not matter.
For every $C$ and every $a>0$ the re-timing $(a,a,C/a)$ is an equivalence with identical statistics, so the unit of $\lambda$ is not detectable for any $C$.

A common shift $\lambda_k\to\lambda_k+\mu$ equals the change of start $\Psi_0\to e^{-iC\mu}\Psi_0$; for an eigenvector start no statistics change and a single-event schedule does not depend on its $\lambda$.

For readings at $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$ the marginal at $\lambda_1$ never depends on the later reading, while the marginal at $\lambda_2$ changes by $\Delta_t=\langle\Psi_1\vert\sum_s\Pi_s[Q_t,\Pi_s]\vert\Psi_1\rangle$, which vanishes for every start iff $[Q_t,\Pi_s]=0$ for all $s,t$.
$C$ is split if $C=F_1+F_2$ with self-adjoint $F_i$, $[F_1,F_2]=0$, $[F_1,\Pi']=0$ and $[F_2,\Pi]=0$ for all place projectors $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P_1$ and $\Pi'$ of $\mathcal P_2$.
For split $C$: $[\Pi(\lambda),\Pi'(\lambda')]=0$ for all $\lambda,\lambda'\ge0$, and $(a_1,a_2,F_1/a_1+F_2/a_2)$ is an equivalence for all $a_1,a_2>0$ whenever this contract is a sum of pair terms.
For uncoupled parts $(a_1,a_2,C_1\otimes\mathbb 1/a_1+\mathbb 1\otimes C_2/a_2)$ is an equivalence for all $a_1,a_2>0$ and every start, so the common now is not detectable.

Two events on different parts with $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$ get equal values iff $a_i/a_j=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ and reversed order iff $a_i/a_j>\lambda_2/\lambda_1$; for uncoupled parts such equivalences exist iff $\lambda_1>0$.

Single-event schedules agree for every start iff $e^{iC\lambda}\Pi e^{-iC\lambda}=e^{ia_iC'\lambda}\Pi e^{-ia_iC'\lambda}$ for all $\lambda\ge0$ and all place projectors $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P_i$, $i=1,2$.
First-order condition: $[C-a_iC',\Pi]=0$ for every place projector $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P_i$.
Second-order condition: $[C,[C,\Pi]]=a_i^2[C',[C',\Pi]]$ for every place projector $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P_i$.
Given the first-order condition, the second-order condition is $[[C,C'],\Pi]=0$, and for both parts together it is $[C,C']=0$.
With the decomposition by transition kind, the first-order conditions read $C'^{(1)}=C^{(1)}/a_1$, $C'^{(2)}=C^{(2)}/a_2$, $C'^{(12)}=C^{(12)}/a_1=C^{(12)}/a_2$, with $C'^{\rm d}$ free.

$(a_1,a_2,C')$ is an equivalence of $C$ iff $[C-a_iC',\Pi]=0$ for all place projectors of $\mathcal P_i$ ($i=1,2$) and $[C,C']=0$; an equivalence with $a_1\neq a_2$ exists iff $C$ is split with $F_2$ a sum of pair terms.
$(a,a,C')$ is an equivalence of $C$ iff $C'=C/a+D$ with $D$ real diagonal in the joint places and $[C,D]=0$.
If $C^{(12)}\neq0$ or $[C^{(1)},C^{(2)}]\neq0$, every equivalence has $a_1=a_2$ and the common now is detectable (sufficient, not necessary).
For $C=g\,\sigma^x\otimes\sigma^x$ all equivalences are $(a,a,C/a+c\,\mathbb 1+\mu\,\sigma^z\otimes\sigma^z)$; the common now is detectable.

For $C=g\,\sigma^z\otimes\sigma^z+h\,\sigma^x\otimes\mathbb 1$ all equivalences are $(a_1,a_2,C/a_1+c\,\mathbb 1+\mu\,\mathbb 1\otimes\sigma^z)$ with arbitrary $a_1,a_2>0$; the common now is not detectable.
For $C=t\,\sigma^x\otimes\mathbb 1+\kappa\,\lvert2\rangle\langle2\rvert\otimes\sigma^x$ all equivalences are $(a,a,C/a+c\,\mathbb 1)$; the common now is detectable.
$P=\tilde P$ for every start iff $[Q_t,\Pi_s]=0$ for all $s,t$ iff $R_i$ influences $R_j$ for no start.
$\sum_s(P(s,t)-\tilde P(s,t))=\Delta_t$, hence $\delta P\le\sum_{s,t}\lvert P(s,t)-\tilde P(s,t)\rvert$ for every start.

$\sum_{s,t}\lvert P-\tilde P\rvert\le\Theta_{mm'}\sum_{k\ge r}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^k/k!\le\Theta_{mm'}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^r e^{2\lVert J\rVert\delta}/r!$ with $\Theta_{mm'}=\tfrac12\sqrt{mm'}(\sqrt m+\sqrt{m'})$, for every start.
The bound is below $\epsilon$ on $\tilde{\mathcal S}_\epsilon=\mathcal S_{2\epsilon/\Theta_{mm'}}=\{0\le\delta<\delta_{2\epsilon/\Theta_{mm'}}(r)\}$, a subset of $\mathcal S_\epsilon$ for $m,m'\ge2$.

For $\delta\le r/(2e^2\lVert J\rVert)$: $\sum_{s,t}\lvert P-\tilde P\rvert\le\Theta_{mm'}e^{-(1-e^{-2})r}$, so $(r,\delta)\in\tilde{\mathcal S}_\epsilon$ if also $r>\ln(\Theta_{mm'}/\epsilon)/(1-e^{-2})$.

class-number constant of the order bound
region of undetectable order to accuracy epsilon

open_issues: Not split is an exact criterion for a detectable common now, but it is not turned into an explicit classification of coupled contracts (out of scope); for more than two objects the proviso that F_2 is a sum of pair terms is part of the criterion.
Item 2 treats two events on different parts; whether the direction can be detected when no reading on one part influences a reading on the other (split C) was not examined.
The order-exchanged statistics is the comparator defined in the question, not the statistics of a schedule; item 5(c) refers to this notion, and the constant Θ in (10.22) is not optimized.
Re-timings that are not linear in λ, more than two parts and readings represented by records are out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions (C λ dimensionless, a_i pure numbers) and C = 0: (10.14) gives all (a_1, a_2, D) with D real diagonal, in agreement with constant place projectors under a diagonal contract.

Contract diagonal in the places, C = g σz⊗σz (coupled): all (a_1, a_2, D) are equivalences, common now not detectable, in agreement with the split F_1 = C, F_2 = 0 and with (10.1); the commutators vanish while the bound (10.22) stays positive.

Example (i) against the exact evolution of two cells: (1⊗σz)(δ) = cos(2gδ) 1⊗σz + sin(2gδ) σx⊗σy reproduces the influence used in Step 3, gives Σ|P − P̃| = sin²(2gδ) ≤ 2√2 (e^{2gδ} − 1) for the start |11⟩ with zero influence, and is unchanged under the equivalences (10.17).
